title: Tribal Movements Jaintia And Garo Rebellion
definition: The Jaintia and Garo rebellions were 19th-century anti-colonial tribal uprisings in the North-East Frontier region, primarily triggered by British administrative encroachment, taxation, and interference in traditional socio-political autonomy.
importanceInUpsc: These movements are critical for understanding the 'Peripheral Resistance' against British expansionism, the transition from traditional tribal governance to colonial administration, and the socio-economic impact of the House Tax and Income Tax in the North-East.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Tribal Movements Jaintia And Garo Rebellion.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
